questions.q: Why is the learning rate usually considered the highest-leverage PPO hyperparameter to tune first?
options: Because it has no effect on training stability
Because even with clipping in place, a too-high learning rate still means each update is poorly aimed, while too low wastes time needlessly
Because it determines the size of the replay buffer
Because it is the only hyperparameter Stable-Baselines3 exposes
questions.explain: Clipping limits how far a single update can push the policy, but it doesn't fix a poorly aimed update caused by too large a learning rate; too small a rate, conversely, just slows convergence.

questions.q: What is the standard default value for PPO's clip_range (epsilon), and when should it typically be changed?
options: 0.99, and it should be changed constantly
0.2, and it rarely needs tuning — a persistently pinned clip_fraction usually points to the learning rate instead
1.0, and it should never be changed
0.0, and it should be increased immediately
questions.explain: 0.2 is the standard default from the original PPO paper. If clip_fraction looks unhealthy, the lesson recommends checking the learning rate first rather than immediately adjusting epsilon.

questions.q: What is the tradeoff involved in choosing n_steps (rollout length)?
options: There is no tradeoff; longer is always strictly better
Too short increases variance in GAE's advantage estimates; too long means the policy drifts further from the one that collected early data in the rollout
n_steps only affects the discount factor
n_steps determines the clip_range automatically
questions.explain: A short rollout gives GAE less data to average over (more variance), while a long rollout risks violating the on-policy assumption as the policy drifts during collection.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which hyperparameters are usually fine left at their standard defaults?
options: Learning rate and clip_range
gamma (0.99), GAE lambda (0.95), and the entropy coefficient, unless a specific symptom points to adjusting them
n_steps and batch size
None of the hyperparameters have reasonable defaults
questions.explain: Gamma, GAE's lambda, and the entropy coefficient are described as near-universal defaults that rarely need adjustment except in direct response to a specific observed symptom.

questions.q: What is the recommended approach to tuning PPO hyperparameters, according to this lesson?
options: Randomly try different values until something works
Start from standard defaults (close to Stable-Baselines3's own), then adjust only the specific hyperparameter that a logged metric's symptom points to
Always maximize the learning rate for fastest training
Change all hyperparameters simultaneously after every failed run
questions.explain: The lesson recommends starting from well-tested defaults and making targeted adjustments based on specific symptoms observed in metrics like approx_kl, clip_fraction, explained_variance, and entropy, rather than guessing in advance.
